rows.basis: The MD&A segment table gives HPC & AI net revenue of $3,192m for FY2022, which matches the sum of the four quarterly HPC & AI figures (790 + 710 + 830 + 862). That is 3,192 ÷ 28,496 = 11.2% of revenue. The line includes traditional HPC and supercomputing as well as AI, so it is an upper bound on AI revenue.

HPC & AI segment revenue was $3,913m, or 13.4% of $29,135m. The quarterly release figures (1.1bn + 840m + 836m + 1.2bn) are rounded and not summed. The segment includes non-AI HPC and supercomputing, so this overstates AI revenue.

From FY2024, HPC & AI is folded into the Server segment ($16,104m, or 53.5% of $30,127m). Server is a data-center line that includes ProLiant and other non-AI servers, so it is a ceiling and not comparable with the FY2022–FY2023 HPC & AI rows. The FY2024 release only says, without an amount, that AI systems revenue 'more than doubled from the prior quarter'.

Server segment revenue was $17,745m, or 51.7% of $34,296m. This is a data-center line that includes non-AI servers, so it is a ceiling. AI systems revenue for the year is not disclosed. The roughly $6.8bn of FY2025 AI systems orders reported in call coverage are orders, are not in the pack, and are not used.
The MD&A says the opex increase was 'primarily due to higher investments in research and development which focus on high-performance computing and AI solutions'. No amount or share is given.
The MD&A says total R&D expense rose $304m (14.9%), 'led by Intelligent Edge, HPC & AI and Storage'. It does not split out the HPC & AI portion.
